verses.text: Nihil ergo nunc damnatiónis est iis, qui sunt in Christo Jesu, qui non secúndum carnem ámbulant.
Lex enim spíritus vitæ in Christo Jesu liberávit me a lege peccáti et mortis.
Nam quod impossíbile erat legi, in quo infirmabátur per carnem: Deus Fílium suum mittens in similitúdinem carnis peccáti, et de peccáto damnávit peccátum in carne,
Ut justificátio legis implerétur in nobis, qui non secúndum carnem ambulámus, sed secúndum spíritum.

responsory.text: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: ecce de quo dicébam vobis: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est:
responsory.repeat: Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

responsory.text: Qui de terra est, de terra lóquitur: qui de cælo venit, super omnes est.
Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

parts.title: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

verses.text: There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh.
For the law of the spirit of life, in Christ Jesus, hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death.
For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh; God sending his own Son, in the likeness of sinful flesh and of sin, hath condemned sin in the flesh;
That the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.

responsory.text: Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me
responsory.repeat: Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

responsory.text: He that is of the earth speaketh of the earth; He That cometh from heaven is above all.
Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

verses.text: Qui enim secúndum carnem sunt: quæ carnis sunt, sápiunt. Qui vero secúndum spíritum sunt, quæ sunt spíritus, séntiunt.
Nam prudéntia carnis, mors est: prudéntia autem spíritus, vita et pax.
Quóniam sapiéntia carnis inimíca est Deo: legi enim Dei non est subjécta: nec enim potest.
Qui autem in carne sunt, Deo placére non possunt.
Vos autem in carne non estis, sed in spíritu: si tamen Spíritus Dei hábitat in vobis.

responsory.text: Dies sanctificátus illúxit nobis: veníte, gentes, et adoráte Dóminum:
responsory.repeat: Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

responsory.text: Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

verses.text: For they that are according to the flesh, mind the things that are of the flesh; but they that are according to the spirit, mind the things that are of the spirit.
For the wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace.
Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be.
And they who are in the flesh, cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you.

responsory.text: This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord.
responsory.repeat: For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

responsory.text: This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

verses.text: Si quis autem Spíritum Christi non habet: hic non est ejus.
Si autem Christus in vobis est: corpus quidem mórtuum est propter peccátum, spíritus vero vivit propter justificatiónem.
Quod si Spíritus ejus, qui suscitávit Jesum a mórtuis, hábitat in vobis: qui suscitávit Jesum Christum a mórtuis, vivificábit, et mortália córpora vestra, propter inhabitántem Spíritum ejus in vobis.

responsory.text: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini, Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis:
Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Allelúja, allelúja.

verses.text: Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
And if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead, because of sin; but the spirit liveth, because of justification.

And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

responsory.text: Blessed be He That cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord Who hath showed us light.
This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
Alleluia, Alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Alleluia, Alleluia.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
paragraphs: Dóminus noster Jesus Christus, fratres caríssimi, qui in ætérnum est cunctórum Creátor, hódie de matre nascéndo factus est nobis Salvátor. Natus est nobis hódie in témpore per voluntátem, ut nos perdúcat ad Patris æternitátem. Factus est Deus homo, ut homo fíeret Deus: ut panem Angelórum manducáret homo, Dóminus Angelórum hódie factus est homo.

responsory.text: Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum:
responsory.repeat: Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

responsory.text: Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

parts.title: A sermon of St. Augustine, Bishop.
paragraphs: Our Lord Jesus Christ, dearest brethren, who in eternity is the Creator of all things, was as at this time born of a mother and became our Saviour. It was as at this time that he willed to be born for us in earthly time, so as to lead us to the Father's eternity. God is made man, that man may be made as God. That man may eat Angels' food, the Lord of Angels was as on this day made man.

responsory.text: Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord.
responsory.repeat: For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

responsory.text: All generations shall call me blessed, for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.
For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

paragraphs: Hódie impléta est prophetía illa, quæ dicit: Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum: aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem. Factus est ígitur qui fécerat, ut invenirétur qui períerat. Sic enim in Psalmis homo confitétur: Priúsquam humiliárer, ego peccávi. Peccávit homo, et factus est reus: natus est homo Deus, ut liberarétur reus. Homo ígitur cécidit, sed Deus descéndit. Cécidit homo miserabíliter, descéndit Deus misericórditer; cécidit homo per supérbiam, descéndit Deus cum grátia.

responsory.text: Confirmátum est cor Vírginis, in quo divína mystéria, Angelo nuntiánte, concépit: tunc speciósum forma præ fíliis hóminum castis suscépit viscéribus:
responsory.repeat: Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

responsory.text: Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.
Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

paragraphs: Now is fulfilled that prophecy: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and bring forth a Saviour. He who made all things is therefore himself made, that those who are lost may be found. It is even as man is made to testify of himself in the Psalms: Before I was humbled, I went wrong. Man sinned and became guilty. God is born man, that the guilty may be delivered. Man fell, but God descended. Man fell miserably, God descended mercifully. Man fell by pride, God descended with grace.

responsory.text: The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men.
responsory.repeat: And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

responsory.text: Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.
And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

paragraphs: O mirácula, o prodígia, fratres mei! Natúræ jura mutántur in hómine; Deus náscitur, virgo sine viro gravidátur, viri nésciam sermo Dei marítat: simul facta est mater et virgo; mater facta, sed incorrúpta; virgo habens fílium, nésciens virum; semper clausa, sed non infœcúnda. Solus enim sine peccáto est natus, quem sine viríli compléxu non concupiscéntia carnis, sed obediéntia génuit mentis.

responsory.text: Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María, quæ sine tactu pudóris invénta es mater Salvatóris:
responsory.repeat: Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

responsory.text: Dómine, audívi audítum tuum, et tímui: considerávi ópera tua, et expávi: in médio duórum animálium.
Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

paragraphs: O my brethren, what a miracle! what a wonder! The laws of nature are changed concerning man: God is born, a Virgin conceiveth without an husband; the Word of God is wedded to one who knoweth no man; she is at once Mother and Virgin. A Mother, yet inviolate: a Virgin having a Son; knowing no man, ever sealed, yet not unfruitful. For he alone was born without sin. He alone was born without human embrace, begotten not of the will of the flesh, but of the obedience of the mind.

responsory.text: Blessed and worshipful art thou, O Virgin Mary; from thee, still maiden undefiled, the Saviour came a little Child.
responsory.repeat: He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

responsory.text: O Lord, I have heard thy speech and was afraid; I considered thy works and trembled. O Thou That dwellest between the two living creatures!
He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Defúncto Heróde, ecce, Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim, qui quærébant ánimam Pueri. Qui consúrgens, accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël. Audiens autem, quod Archeláus regnáret in Judæa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire: et, admonítus in somnis, secéssit in partes Galilææ. Et véniens habitávit in civitáte, quæ vocátur Názareth: ut adimplére tur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazaræus vocábitur.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri
parts.source: Liber 1 in Comment. in cap. 2 Matthæi
paragraphs: Ex hoc loco intellígimus non solum Heródem, sed et sacerdótes et scribas eódem témpore necem Dómini fuísse meditátos. Qui surgens accépit púerum, et matrem ejus. Non dixit: Accépit fílium suum et uxórem suam, sed Púerum et matrem ejus; quasi nutrítius, non marítus.

responsory.text: Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio:
responsory.repeat: Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.

responsory.text: Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

parts.title: Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)
parts.source: Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.
paragraphs: From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

responsory.text: O Mary, how holy and how spotless is thy virginity! I am too dull to praise thee!
responsory.repeat: For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

responsory.text: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

paragraphs: Audiens autem quod Archeláus regnáret in Judǽa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire. Multi labúntur erróre propter ignorántiam históriæ, putántes eumdem esse Heródem, a quo in passióne sua Dóminus irridétur, et qui nunc mórtuus esse referátur. Ergo Heródes ille qui cum Piláto póstea amicítias fecit, hujus Heródis fílius est, frater Archelái.

responsory.text: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre:
responsory.repeat: Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

responsory.text: Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.
Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

paragraphs: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

responsory.text: The Virgin-Mother that knew not a man, bore, but travailed not.
responsory.repeat: She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

responsory.text: Soon rises in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine; The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.
She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

paragraphs: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur. Si fixum de Scriptúris posuísset exémplum, numquam díceret: Quod dictum est per prophétas: sed simplíciter: Quod dictum est per prophétam. Nunc autem pluráliter prophétas vocans, osténdit se non verba de Scriptúris sumpsísse, sed sensum. Nazarǽus sanctus interpretátur; sanctum autem Dóminum futúrum omnis Scriptúra commémorat.

He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

latin.heading: Octávo Idus Januárii Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
entries: Floréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ejus autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.
Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.

In território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, jubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.
Rhédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, júgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.
Geris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.
latin.closing: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

translation.heading: January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon
entries: The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.
Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.
On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).
At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).
translation.closing: And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

email.subject: Matins for Tuesday 5 January: Vigil of the Epiphany
email.preheader: There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh.
email.html:
There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh.

Matins · Tuesday, 5 January 2027

Vigil of the Epiphany

In Vigilia Epiphaniæ · Semiduplex

Commemoration: St. Telesphorus, Pope and Martyr

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 8:1-4

There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh. For the law of the spirit of life, in Christ Jesus, hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death. For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh; God sending his own Son, in the likeness of sinful flesh and of sin, hath condemned sin in the flesh; That the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.

℟. Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me * Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

℣. He that is of the earth speaketh of the earth; He That cometh from heaven is above all.

℟. Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

Lesson II

Rom 8:5-9

For they that are according to the flesh, mind the things that are of the flesh; but they that are according to the spirit, mind the things that are of the spirit. For the wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace. Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be. And they who are in the flesh, cannot please God. But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you.

℟. This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord. * For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

Lesson III

Rom 8:9-11

Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. And if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead, because of sin; but the spirit liveth, because of justification. And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

℟. Blessed be He That cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord Who hath showed us light. * Alleluia, Alleluia.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Lesson IV

A sermon of St. Augustine, Bishop.

Serm. 13. de Tempore.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, dearest brethren, who in eternity is the Creator of all things, was as at this time born of a mother and became our Saviour. It was as at this time that he willed to be born for us in earthly time, so as to lead us to the Father's eternity. God is made man, that man may be made as God. That man may eat Angels' food, the Lord of Angels was as on this day made man.

℟. Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord. * For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

℣. All generations shall call me blessed, for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.

℟. For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

Lesson V

Now is fulfilled that prophecy: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and bring forth a Saviour. He who made all things is therefore himself made, that those who are lost may be found. It is even as man is made to testify of himself in the Psalms: Before I was humbled, I went wrong. Man sinned and became guilty. God is born man, that the guilty may be delivered. Man fell, but God descended. Man fell miserably, God descended mercifully. Man fell by pride, God descended with grace.

℟. The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men. * And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

℣. Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

Lesson VI

O my brethren, what a miracle! what a wonder! The laws of nature are changed concerning man: God is born, a Virgin conceiveth without an husband; the Word of God is wedded to one who knoweth no man; she is at once Mother and Virgin. A Mother, yet inviolate: a Virgin having a Son; knowing no man, ever sealed, yet not unfruitful. For he alone was born without sin. He alone was born without human embrace, begotten not of the will of the flesh, but of the obedience of the mind.

℟. Blessed and worshipful art thou, O Virgin Mary; from thee, still maiden undefiled, the Saviour came a little Child. * He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℣. O Lord, I have heard thy speech and was afraid; I considered thy works and trembled. O Thou That dwellest between the two living creatures!

℟. He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

Lesson VII

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 2:19-23

In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)

Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.

From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

℟. O Mary, how holy and how spotless is thy virginity! I am too dull to praise thee! * For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

℣. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

℟. For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

Lesson VIII

But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

℟. The Virgin-Mother that knew not a man, bore, but travailed not. * She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

℣. Soon rises in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine; The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

Lesson IX

He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

Te Deum

Martyrology

Read at Prime today, announcing tomorrow

January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon

The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.

Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.

On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).

At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

℟. Thanks be to God.

Read in Latin and English

Roman Breviary, Divino Afflatu, with the additions to 1962. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).

page.title: Matins for Tuesday, 5 January 2027: Vigil of the Epiphany
page.html:
Tuesday, 5 January 2027

In Vigilia EpiphaniæVigil of the Epiphany

Semiduplex

Commemoratio: S. Telesphori Papæ et Martyris

Commemoration: St. Telesphorus, Pope and Martyr

Lectio I

Lesson I

De Epístola ad Romános

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 8:1-4

Rom 8:1-4

Nihil ergo nunc damnatiónis est iis, qui sunt in Christo Jesu, qui non secúndum carnem ámbulant. Lex enim spíritus vitæ in Christo Jesu liberávit me a lege peccáti et mortis. Nam quod impossíbile erat legi, in quo infirmabátur per carnem: Deus Fílium suum mittens in similitúdinem carnis peccáti, et de peccáto damnávit peccátum in carne, Ut justificátio legis implerétur in nobis, qui non secúndum carnem ambulámus, sed secúndum spíritum.

There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh. For the law of the spirit of life, in Christ Jesus, hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death. For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh; God sending his own Son, in the likeness of sinful flesh and of sin, hath condemned sin in the flesh; That the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.

℟. Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: ecce de quo dicébam vobis: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est: * Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

℟. Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me * Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

℣. Qui de terra est, de terra lóquitur: qui de cælo venit, super omnes est.

℣. He that is of the earth speaketh of the earth; He That cometh from heaven is above all.

℟. Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

℟. Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

Lectio II

Lesson II

Rom 8:5-9

Rom 8:5-9

Qui enim secúndum carnem sunt: quæ carnis sunt, sápiunt. Qui vero secúndum spíritum sunt, quæ sunt spíritus, séntiunt. Nam prudéntia carnis, mors est: prudéntia autem spíritus, vita et pax. Quóniam sapiéntia carnis inimíca est Deo: legi enim Dei non est subjécta: nec enim potest. Qui autem in carne sunt, Deo placére non possunt. Vos autem in carne non estis, sed in spíritu: si tamen Spíritus Dei hábitat in vobis.

For they that are according to the flesh, mind the things that are of the flesh; but they that are according to the spirit, mind the things that are of the spirit. For the wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace. Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be. And they who are in the flesh, cannot please God. But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you.

℟. Dies sanctificátus illúxit nobis: veníte, gentes, et adoráte Dóminum: * Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

℟. This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord. * For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

℣. Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

℟. For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

Lectio III

Lesson III

Rom 8:9-11

Rom 8:9-11

Si quis autem Spíritum Christi non habet: hic non est ejus. Si autem Christus in vobis est: corpus quidem mórtuum est propter peccátum, spíritus vero vivit propter justificatiónem. Quod si Spíritus ejus, qui suscitávit Jesum a mórtuis, hábitat in vobis: qui suscitávit Jesum Christum a mórtuis, vivificábit, et mortália córpora vestra, propter inhabitántem Spíritum ejus in vobis.

Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. And if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead, because of sin; but the spirit liveth, because of justification. And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

℟. Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini, Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis: * Allelúja, allelúja.

℟. Blessed be He That cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord Who hath showed us light. * Alleluia, Alleluia.

℣. Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. Allelúja, allelúja.

℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Allelúja, allelúja.

℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Lectio IV

Lesson IV

Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi

A sermon of St. Augustine, Bishop.

Sermo 13 de Tempore

Serm. 13. de Tempore.

Dóminus noster Jesus Christus, fratres caríssimi, qui in ætérnum est cunctórum Creátor, hódie de matre nascéndo factus est nobis Salvátor. Natus est nobis hódie in témpore per voluntátem, ut nos perdúcat ad Patris æternitátem. Factus est Deus homo, ut homo fíeret Deus: ut panem Angelórum manducáret homo, Dóminus Angelórum hódie factus est homo.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, dearest brethren, who in eternity is the Creator of all things, was as at this time born of a mother and became our Saviour. It was as at this time that he willed to be born for us in earthly time, so as to lead us to the Father's eternity. God is made man, that man may be made as God. That man may eat Angels' food, the Lord of Angels was as on this day made man.

℟. Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum: * Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

℟. Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord. * For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

℣. Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.

℣. All generations shall call me blessed, for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.

℟. Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

℟. For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

Lectio V

Lesson V

Hódie impléta est prophetía illa, quæ dicit: Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum: aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem. Factus est ígitur qui fécerat, ut invenirétur qui períerat. Sic enim in Psalmis homo confitétur: Priúsquam humiliárer, ego peccávi. Peccávit homo, et factus est reus: natus est homo Deus, ut liberarétur reus. Homo ígitur cécidit, sed Deus descéndit. Cécidit homo miserabíliter, descéndit Deus misericórditer; cécidit homo per supérbiam, descéndit Deus cum grátia.

Now is fulfilled that prophecy: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and bring forth a Saviour. He who made all things is therefore himself made, that those who are lost may be found. It is even as man is made to testify of himself in the Psalms: Before I was humbled, I went wrong. Man sinned and became guilty. God is born man, that the guilty may be delivered. Man fell, but God descended. Man fell miserably, God descended mercifully. Man fell by pride, God descended with grace.

℟. Confirmátum est cor Vírginis, in quo divína mystéria, Angelo nuntiánte, concépit: tunc speciósum forma præ fíliis hóminum castis suscépit viscéribus: * Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

℟. The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men. * And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

℣. Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.

℣. Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

℟. And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

O mirácula, o prodígia, fratres mei! Natúræ jura mutántur in hómine; Deus náscitur, virgo sine viro gravidátur, viri nésciam sermo Dei marítat: simul facta est mater et virgo; mater facta, sed incorrúpta; virgo habens fílium, nésciens virum; semper clausa, sed non infœcúnda. Solus enim sine peccáto est natus, quem sine viríli compléxu non concupiscéntia carnis, sed obediéntia génuit mentis.

O my brethren, what a miracle! what a wonder! The laws of nature are changed concerning man: God is born, a Virgin conceiveth without an husband; the Word of God is wedded to one who knoweth no man; she is at once Mother and Virgin. A Mother, yet inviolate: a Virgin having a Son; knowing no man, ever sealed, yet not unfruitful. For he alone was born without sin. He alone was born without human embrace, begotten not of the will of the flesh, but of the obedience of the mind.

℟. Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María, quæ sine tactu pudóris invénta es mater Salvatóris: * Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

℟. Blessed and worshipful art thou, O Virgin Mary; from thee, still maiden undefiled, the Saviour came a little Child. * He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℣. Dómine, audívi audítum tuum, et tímui: considerávi ópera tua, et expávi: in médio duórum animálium.

℣. O Lord, I have heard thy speech and was afraid; I considered thy works and trembled. O Thou That dwellest between the two living creatures!

℟. Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

℟. He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

℟. He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 2:19-23

Matt 2:19-23

In illo témpore: Defúncto Heróde, ecce, Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim, qui quærébant ánimam Pueri. Qui consúrgens, accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël. Audiens autem, quod Archeláus regnáret in Judæa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire: et, admonítus in somnis, secéssit in partes Galilææ. Et véniens habitávit in civitáte, quæ vocátur Názareth: ut adimplére tur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazaræus vocábitur.

In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)

Liber 1 in Comment. in cap. 2 Matthæi

Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.

Ex hoc loco intellígimus non solum Heródem, sed et sacerdótes et scribas eódem témpore necem Dómini fuísse meditátos. Qui surgens accépit púerum, et matrem ejus. Non dixit: Accépit fílium suum et uxórem suam, sed Púerum et matrem ejus; quasi nutrítius, non marítus.

From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

℟. Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio: * Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.

℟. O Mary, how holy and how spotless is thy virginity! I am too dull to praise thee! * For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

℣. Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.

℣. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

℟. Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Audiens autem quod Archeláus regnáret in Judǽa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire. Multi labúntur erróre propter ignorántiam históriæ, putántes eumdem esse Heródem, a quo in passióne sua Dóminus irridétur, et qui nunc mórtuus esse referátur. Ergo Heródes ille qui cum Piláto póstea amicítias fecit, hujus Heródis fílius est, frater Archelái.

But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

℟. Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre: * Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

℟. The Virgin-Mother that knew not a man, bore, but travailed not. * She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

℣. Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.

℣. Soon rises in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine; The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Lectio IX

Lesson IX

Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur. Si fixum de Scriptúris posuísset exémplum, numquam díceret: Quod dictum est per prophétas: sed simplíciter: Quod dictum est per prophétam. Nunc autem pluráliter prophétas vocans, osténdit se non verba de Scriptúris sumpsísse, sed sensum. Nazarǽus sanctus interpretátur; sanctum autem Dóminum futúrum omnis Scriptúra commémorat.

He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

Epiphánia Dómini.

Floréntiæ natális sancti Andréæ Corsíni, civis Florentíni, ex Ordine Carmelitárum, Epíscopi Fesuláni et Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Urbánus Papa Octávus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ejus autem festívitas recólitur prídie Nonas Februárii.

Barcinóne, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Raymúndi de Peñáfort, ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus vero festum décimo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.

In Africa commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Sevéri, ad palum ligáti sunt et igne consúmpti.

In território Rheménsi pássio sanctæ Macræ Vírginis, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, jubénte Rictiováro Prǽside, cum in ignem esset præcipitáta et permansísset illǽsa, dehinc, mamíllis abscíssis et squalóre cárceris afflícta, super testas étiam acutíssimas ac prunas volutáta, tandem orans migrávit ad Dóminum.

Rhédonis, in Gállia, sancti Melánii, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, post innumerabílium signa virtútum, júgiter cælo inténtus, gloriósus migrávit a sǽculo.

Geris, in Ægýpto, sancti Nilammónis reclúsi, qui, dum ad Episcopátum traherétur invítus, in oratióne spíritum Deo réddidit.

℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

Martyrology

Read at Prime today, announcing tomorrow

January 6th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon

The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.

Upon the same 6th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Florence, holy Andrew Corsini of that city, a Carmelite friar, Bishop of Fiesoli, who was famous for miracles (in the year 1373), and whose name was numbered by Urban VIII. among those of the Saints, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of February.

At Barcelona (in the year 1275), holy Raymond of Pehafuerte, of the order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, whose feast we keep upon the 23rd day of this present month of January.

On the same day are commemorated many holy martyrs in Africa, who were burnt at the stake in the persecution under the Emperor Severus.

In the country of Reims, by command of the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy virgin and martyr Macra she was first cast into the fire but remained unhurt, whereupon her breasts were cut off, and she was thrust into a prison and rolled upon sharp potsherds and live coals until she passed away in prayer to be ever with the Lord.

At Rennes, in Gaul, the holy confessor Melanius (Abbot of Platz) (in the year 511), bishop of that see, who after countless works of power passed gloriously out of this world to that heaven where his heart was already fixed (in the year 530).

At Geris, in Egypt, the holy hermit Nilammon, who gave up his soul in prayer to God while he was being haled against his will to make him a bishop (fifth century).

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

℟. Thanks be to God.
